windows.hook_title: That Avocado Came From a 700-Year-Old Tree
windows.transcript_excerpt: That's pretty good avocado. Wow. That's pretty solid. That's perfect. Oh, you know, it's crazy about that avocado. So that was from an avocado tree that was 700 years old.
windows.why_it_works: TOP PICK of the as-run library (score 92). Opens mid-taste on a genuine reaction ('That's pretty good avocado. Wow. That's pretty solid. That's perfect.'), then lands a concrete, surprising reveal inside the window: the avocado came from a tree '700 years old'. One complete idea, a specific number as the payoff, no context needed before second 0.

windows.hook_title: Wagyu Cows Get Jazz Massages For 30 Years
windows.why_it_works: Score 90 in the as-run library. The hook is an absurd-but-specific production detail - the wagyu cows behind the $10,000 end of the comparison get jazz massages, for 30 years - the kind of concrete, repeatable fact a viewer quotes to someone else. Fits the source's $1-vs-$10,000 contrast spine. Reason rests on the fixture hook title; no transcript for this range is cached in-tree.

windows.transcript_excerpt: I'm talking like $400 per sandwich, like USD dollars? ... So 400 for like this right here? Yeah, but there's like three. ... Oh, I didn't mention there's gold. Real gold.
windows.why_it_works: Textbook hook-to-payoff arc in 25 s. Opens on the price question itself ('I'm talking like $400 per sandwich, like USD dollars?'), runs a short disbelief negotiation, and ends on a second reveal held back until the last seconds: 'Oh, I didn't mention there's gold. Real gold.' The ending is the payoff, not a fade-out.

windows.transcript_excerpt: Kobe sandwich. ... There's a little gold in your water. So this is the dry ace and this is the one... Yeah, look at that. I mean, take a look at that right there. I mean, look, it's like... It's talking to me. It says eat, bro.
windows.why_it_works: The presentation-and-reaction peak of the $10,000 course: the Kobe sandwich arrives ('There's a little gold in your water'), and the reaction escalates on camera - 'take a look at that right there... It's talking to me. It says eat, bro.' Energy and a quotable line carry it; the window contains the full build from reveal to reaction.

Pure price-shock arithmetic as the hook: four pieces of sushi, $400 - a specific count against a specific price, instantly graspable in the first seconds and self-contained. Reason rests on the fixture hook title; no transcript for this range is cached in-tree.

windows.why_it_fails: The g1 moment shifted +8 s. Overlaps the gold by 60% of the gold's length, so a selector returning both this and g1 spends two picks on one moment (the rubric's dedupe step exists to collapse exactly this), and the shift drags in 8 s of post-reveal tail.

Starts at 15:00, mid-reveal: the first words are '700 years old. No' with the subject (the avocado tree) only established in the seconds before. Fails hard gate (a) - the first sentence needs the missing context - even though it overlaps the gold.

Same open as the gold but ends at 14:59, about a second before the '700 years old' reveal lands (transcript puts the reveal at 15:00). All setup, no payoff - fails the rubric's Payoff and Ending components.
